question: Calculate \(103\times97\). (You may use the difference of squares formula to simplify the calculation.)

provenance.contribution: Existing attributed explanation retained; project contribution is review and annotations.
provenance.reviewStatus: Current explanation retained and independently AI-reviewed; not teacher reviewed

solutionMethods.explanation:
Since \(97=100-3\), subtract three groups of \(103\) from one hundred groups of \(103\):
\[
103\times97=103(100-3)=10300-309=9991.
\]
The product is \(9991\).
solutionMethods.label: Subtract three groups

reference.question: Calculate \(103\times97\). (You may use the difference of squares formula to simplify the calculation.)
reference.solution:
Method 1: Difference of squares

\(103\times97=(100+3)(100-3)=100^2-3^2=10000-9=9991\).

Method 2: Subtract three groups

Since \(97=100-3\), subtract three groups of \(103\) from one hundred groups of \(103\):
\[
103\times97=103(100-3)=10300-309=9991.
\]
The product is \(9991\).
